_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. The rout keeps the router's slot grid where its men stood when it broke (#1765), and the router is carried east along the pursuer's front while the pursuer is still on it (about (1044, 657) at tick 440, (1085, 622) at tick 492, its men up against the hill's west face but none inside it), then flees north-west and north (about (967, 474) at tick 560, (979, 237) at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 (ROUTING at 703, IDLE at 704) at about (976, 174), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). It pulls up with its men in step and its heading held on its flight line (-91 degrees): anchor about (976, 159) at tick 710, still coasting at about (975, 132) when the clip ends, so the rally's heading turn and re-square, which wait for the coast to stop, fall after the clip. Its men are off their own slots from the tick after the rout, not from the fight: the mean body-to-slot gap is 19.8 wu at tick 343, 288.9 at tick 344 and 312.8 at tick 352. Its first flight turn, at tick 344 while it is still in contact, is under the 75 degree threshold above which a turn is folded into the grid, so the grid swings round under the men (#1785). The gap is 86.4 wu at tick 703 (298.6 on main 7d209821). The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the router streams out through the pursuer's deep column: the pursuer holds its facing (26 degrees at tick 440) and its slot grid while the router is among its ranks. At tick 483, as the router leaves it, its facing snaps 35 degrees to -13 (under the 75 degree threshold above which a re-face turns in place, so the snap is not folded into its grid, #1806) and its mean body-to-slot gap jumps from 65.4 to 143.0 wu; at tick 504 it re-faces 167 degrees (folded in, the gap unchanged) and stays near the hill's south-west corner (anchor about (1094, 688) at tick 720) rather than riding north after it. A 2-tick scan from the divergence (tick 343) reads the pursuer's sustained shape residual at 102.6 wu against the 30 wu threshold (declared below); on main e81ea9fa it read 13.3 wu, and on main fa76accc, where the grid swung round with the facing and the anchor backed away to the south-east, 142.2 wu (#1757). Before the charge came straight in (rout at tick 469), the same scan from the rout read 75.4 wu: the straight charge did not cause the deformation. The declared checks pin the router's story beats with sparse post-rout samples (400, 560, 680, the rally at 703/704, and 710) rather than sampling the gallop densely. The router's own scramble (judged only on the 16 ticks after its rally) is declared below as an exemption rather than sampled around.

shape_residual.reason: uid 0 (the router): it rallies at tick 704, and the 16 ticks to the clip's end are its only judged samples (a router is not judged). Its men reach the rally off their own slots because of its first flight turn: the mean body-to-slot gap is 19.8 wu at tick 343, the rout, through a fight that kept the block in shape, then 288.9 wu at tick 344 and 312.8 at tick 352. That turn, made while the router is still in contact, is under the 75 degree threshold above which a turn is folded into the grid, so the grid swings round under the men (#1785). Through the judged ticks the block coasts with its heading held, and its re-square waits for the coast to stop, after the clip (86.1 wu at tick 704, 79.4 at tick 720). Sustained shape residual 69.7 wu on 2-tick samples from the divergence (tick 343), against 238.8 wu on main 7d209821. uid 1 (the pursuer), new with #1765: the router now leaves the pursuer's ranks eastward along its front, and at tick 483, as it goes, the pursuer's facing snaps 35 degrees (26 to -13). That is under the same threshold, so its grid swings unfolded and its mean body-to-slot gap jumps from 65.4 to 143.0 wu in one tick (#1806). It never re-forms before the clip ends (88.3 wu at tick 720). From about tick 560 it also stalls by the hill's south-west corner: its anchor is commanded at 145 to 91 wu/s along a path step about 50 degrees off its facing, which it turns towards at about 5 degrees a second, but advances only 0.06 to 0.45 wu a tick, while its men stand 100 to 150 wu off their slots on average. Its body coupling holding the anchor back to its scattered men would explain the stall; that was inferred, not instrumented (#1806). On main it rode north after the router. Sustained shape residual 102.6 wu here, against 13.33 wu on main 7d209821. Both the snap and the stall are tracked in #1806. Measured 2026-10-11.
